title: HTTP sources
summary: Two ways a vendor cloud feeds an adapter over HTTP. A webhook (top) is pushed to the public receiver, which authenticates it and hands it to the tenant's ingress broker. A polling source (bottom) runs inside the tenant runtime and asks the vendor's API on a schedule. Both end as decoder inputs, so the decoder and publisher are the same as for MQTT.

boxes.label: Vendor cloud
boxes.detail: Posts to the adapter's ingest URL, the public address plus `/w/<ingest id>`. The ingest ID is 32 random characters and is not a secret; the delivery still has to authenticate.

boxes.label: Webhook receiver
boxes.detail: A small public HTTP service with no database and no Docker access. It finds the adapter in a routing file that adapter-manager writes whenever Laravel changes a route or secret, and rereads every second. Bodies over 1 MiB, also after decompression, are refused. Deliveries never pass through Laravel.

boxes.label: Authenticate
boxes.sub: HMAC, header token or URL token
boxes.detail: Three modes: an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the body (optionally with a timestamp header, accepted within 5 minutes), a token in a header, or a token as the next URL segment. Up to two secrets are active so one can be rotated. Comparisons are constant-time, and an address with more than 30 failures in a minute is refused for 5 minutes.

boxes.label: Refused
boxes.detail: Every authentication failure answers 401 without saying why. Rate limits answer 429: 10 a second per adapter with a burst of 100, and 50 a second per organization. A paused adapter or an unavailable broker answers 503 with Retry-After. The reason goes to the adapter's Activity in the receiver's next report.

boxes.label: Kept as a sample
boxes.detail: Before a webhook revision is deployed the route is in `sampling`: an authenticated delivery is answered 202 and its first 64 KiB go to Laravel as a sample that can become a decoder fixture. Nothing is decoded or published.

boxes.label: Tenant ingress broker
boxes.detail: The receiver publishes the body with MQTT 5 at QoS 1 as `webhook-<adapter uuid>`, an identity that can only publish to this topic. Path, query, content type, safe headers and a delivery ID travel as user properties. The 202 is sent only after the broker acknowledged.

boxes.label: Webhook source node
boxes.detail: The adapter's source node in webhook mode. It subscribes with a session that survives restarts, rebuilds the request from the user properties as the input's `http` field, and keeps a retained online/offline status the receiver follows. While it is offline the receiver accepts at most 500 deliveries or 32 MiB.

boxes.label: Vendor HTTP API
boxes.detail: Must be HTTPS and resolve only to public addresses; redirects are checked the same way and credentials are not sent to another host. A response is limited to 8 MiB, 30 seconds and 5,000 records.

boxes.label: Polling source node
boxes.sub: Fetch a page, split into records
boxes.detail: The source node in poll mode. On each run it builds a GET or POST from the saved settings, filling placeholders such as `{cursor}` and `{window_start}`, and places the credential as a header, query parameter, bearer token or basic auth. A JSON Pointer says where the records are. One tenant runtime sends at most 60 requests a minute.

boxes.label: Commit the cursor
boxes.detail: The cursor (a timestamp, a token or a time window) is written to the runtime's data volume only when every record of the page was published, found duplicate or recorded as failed. A run takes up to 20 pages by default, then reports itself to Laravel as a poll run.

boxes.label: Retrying or stopped
boxes.detail: 408, 429, 5xx and network errors retry with a doubling delay up to an hour, or after the Retry-After the API gave. Other 4xx answers, a response that is not JSON or is too large, and a missing records location stop the poller until a person resumes it.

edges.label: one input per record, a page at a time

steps.text: A vendor cloud posts to the adapter's ingest URL. The receiver looks the ingest ID up in its routing file and reads the body, up to 1 MiB.
The delivery is authenticated with the adapter's mode: an HMAC signature of the body, a header token or a URL token, against at most two active secrets.
A bad or stale signature answers 401. Past the rate limits it is 429, and for a paused adapter 503. The decoder never sees a refused delivery.
If no webhook revision is deployed yet, the delivery is answered 202 and kept as a sample to write the decoder against.
Otherwise the receiver publishes the body to the adapter's topic on the tenant's ingress broker and answers 202 only when the broker has acknowledged it.
The adapter's source node takes it from its persistent session. If the runtime is restarting, the broker holds the deliveries, up to a bounded backlog.
The decoder gets the body plus an `http` field with the path, query, content type, headers and delivery ID. Secrets and proxy headers are left out.
A polling source has no receiver. Its source node wakes on its interval, between 60 seconds and 24 hours, and requests one page starting at the cursor.
Each record of the page becomes one decoder input. The page is decoded and published before anything else happens.
When every record is settled, the cursor moves and is written to disk. A crash before that fetches the page again; when the decoder returns message IDs, the publisher drops the repeats.
If the API signals more data the next page follows at once; otherwise the run ends and is reported with its counts and cursor.
A temporary error retries with backoff. An error a retry cannot fix, such as rejected credentials, stops the poller until someone resumes it.
